[National Post] Andrew Coyne on electoral reform: Are the Liberals conning us, again?

Coyne has made his opinion on this topic known previously - he doesn't like the idea. I've taken issue with his thoughts [on various topics] many times but since his arguments are usually formed on some form of reasonable logic it's difficult to get too wound up about them, this time his argument seems based on simple hyper-partisan considerations.

His opening paragraph reads,

The question is whether a more democratic end may be achieved by less than democratic means; whether an electoral system that is more responsive to the public may be imposed without meaningfully consulting that same public; whether a more consensual, less partisan politics is the probable result of a fairly naked attempt by one party to control the process from start to finish.

I'll take his points one at a time

The question is whether a more democratic end may be achieved by less than democratic means;

How are we entering a process of "less than democratic means"?

The Liberal Party, with Trudeau at its head, won the last election under the FPTP electoral system championed by Coyne with a major plank of its campaign being the elimination of the FPTP electoral system.

We also see, via iPolitics, that MP's will be asked to hold town hall meetings on the topic in their ridings to gather input from us, the great unwashed electoral masses.

How is any of this "less than democratic"?

whether an electoral system that is more responsive to the public may be imposed without meaningfully consulting that same public;

I am given to wonder if Andrew Coyne

  1. does not read iPolitics,

  2. didn't actually bother to get the details of the LPC plan from House of Commons discussions, or

  3. found the details of the riding by riding consultations with constituents at town hall meetings inconvenient to his point so simply decided to ignore that aspect of the plan and hoped that no one would notice.

There is also the question as to whether or not Coyne also believes that the FPTP system was imposed upon the electorate of the day without meaningful consultation, and is therefore equally lacking in credibility.

whether a more consensual, less partisan politics is the probable result of a fairly naked attempt by one party to control the process from start to finish.

The Liberal Party of Canada, with Trudeau at its head, won the last election and is control of all processes that will pass through the House of Commons for the next 3 1/2 years - exactly as the Conservative Party of Canada, with Harper at its head, was in control of all processes that passed through the House of Commons during the preceding Parliament. This is the way our democracy has worked since Confederation, with Prime Ministers, through the use of their Party Whips, controlling those processes from behind a single desk. It was Stephen Harper himself who said

“Let's face it, the average backbench MP is little more than a bench warmer for his/her political party.”

Is that the democracy that Coyne really believes we should cling to?

The FPTP system creates what can only be described as a faux democracy, it's a system that perpetuates rule by the greatest minority that, through the magic of electoral math, gets to syle itself as a majority - and that is not democratic.

ANY system that provides a Parliament that is more reflective of how Canadians actually vote is a step forward, and I, for one, embrace the change - and you can bet your next pay cheque that when the town hall meetings are held in my riding I will be there in support of that change.
